findings.claim: Completed replays return the stored response before invoking the route service callback, so authorization is not revalidated after access revocation.
Target path values are absent from both idempotency identity and request fingerprint, allowing the same principal, key, and payload on different resource IDs to alias one ledger record.
The forward migration reconciles legacy duplicates only after migration 000003, so a database at 000002 with duplicates can fail at 000003 before 000004 executes.
Creation wrappers generate a fresh default idempotency key on every invocation, so retries without explicitly retained keys are treated as new intents.
Execution examples contain complete local PostgreSQL URLs with embedded username and password.
A database before 000003 with duplicate pending invitations can fail at 000003 before reconciliation in 000004; the migration test bypasses that ordered path.
Idempotency identity omits organization and group target IDs, so key reuse across targets can replay the wrong result or return a false conflict.
Production creation wrappers generate a new default idempotency key per invocation and no production caller retains a key after an ambiguous response.
The fail-closed database contract command omits ./internal/httpapi, so the PostgreSQL idempotency executor suite can regress while the gate succeeds.
The contract script requires no positive named execution markers, and its harness accepts a fake zero-exit go command that prints only PASS.
A downstream panic bypasses both sanitized response handling and the structured failure event because the middleware has no recovery boundary.
Caller-supplied printable X-Request-ID values are copied unchanged into responses and failure logs, allowing sensitive header content to be emitted.
Background idempotency cleanup logs wrapped pgx errors with %v, exposing raw database diagnostics outside the new redaction path.
Expired in_progress rows are neither cleaned nor reclaimed, so the same identity can remain permanently unavailable.
A single 100-row cleanup batch per hour can accumulate expired records when terminal creation volume exceeds cleanup capacity.
Reconciliation updates and index creation have no production row-count, lock-duration, or migration-time evidence.
The production signal has no causal error class, fingerprint, metric, grouping, or alert binding for evaluating error-rate thresholds.
statusWriter advertises optional interfaces even when unsupported and Flush does not record implicit 200 status.
Idempotent-create orchestration is duplicated across five handler branches and the copies already vary in helper and status-constant usage.
RegisterRoutes accepts a variadic executor list but silently uses only the first, obscuring actual cardinality and optionality.
Execute combines validation, transactions, locking, state loading, replay, reclamation, creation, persistence, and commit in one nested function.
IsIdempotentCreationRoute is production code used only by tests and duplicates the route list rather than verifying actual registration.
TestIdempotencyExecutorContract executes no behavior and contains no assertion.
One integration test serially couples many contracts through shared setup, so an early failure hides later contract results.
Organization and idempotency integration suites duplicate PostgreSQL URL, temporary-schema, search-path pool, and cleanup setup.
SafeResult exposes Body as any, so the documented endpoint-specific safe DTO allowlist is not represented by the type contract.
The design includes normalized path UUIDs in canonical identity while implementation uses only the route template and request body.
The retry test manually reuses a low-level key but does not exercise a production creation wrapper or UI retry lifecycle.
Unit 2-4 evidence refers to unspecified Unit results without stable output paths or hashes, limiting reproducibility from the artifact.
The shell harness compresses setup and assertions into compound lines without assertion-specific diagnostics.
Idempotency retention, cleanup, key length, and status policies are scattered numeric literals across Go and SQL.
Parameterized-route idempotency identities omit organization and group path values, allowing cross-target replay for the same principal, key, and payload.
Public creation wrappers generate a new default idempotency key per invocation, so unchanged UI retries receive a new key unless callers retain an optional argument.
The database contract script has no positive execution markers and accepts arbitrary zero-exit output with no executed tests.
The database gate omits ./internal/httpapi, and the idempotency integration test substitutes a hand-built table rather than the production migration schema.
Handler tests never submit successful keyed creation requests, so keyed dispatch, replay DTOs, conflict mapping, and target identity can be broken across all scoped endpoints without test failure.
The reconciliation test skips migration 000003 and therefore does not prove that an ordered upgrade with legacy duplicates reaches 000004.
The target marks visible group-grant refresh coverage complete but adds no behavioral test that creates a group grant and observes refreshed access state.
The owner concurrency test treats any error as a valid rejection and does not assert ErrLastOwner.
Invitation tests omit mixed active/expired listing and test only the ID tie-break rather than newest-created-at duplicate selection.
The error middleware has no panic recovery test or behavior, so a panic escapes before sanitized response and logging.
The restoration test proves login content but does not assert routing state changed to /login.
Coverage includes a no-assertion executor test and an implementation allowlist test unused by production routing.
